title: Cap. X: Justice, conjunction, unknown covenant — stop before Theologorum
pass_a_gloss: But perhaps justice demanded that God will to impute that first sin rather than other sins? Why then, Placeus asks, did Garissoles not bring that cause? Why did he say the unique cause of the matter is God's will? Or how will it be proved — Placeus's side now only answering — that justice demanded it? If you flee to the conjunction between us and Adam, was it greater when he first sinned than afterward, or greater with him than with our nearer parents? If you flee to some unknown covenant whose condition was that if he sinned, his first sin would be imputed to all his posterity unto those two penalties — inherent sin and eternal death — that covenant must be proved from Scripture, which is wholly impossible. We must guard most carefully not to attribute to God anything beyond Scripture, especially anything that darkens His virtues — for that cannot but be a grave sin. Stops before Garissoles joins Whitaker, Chamier, Sixtus of Siena, and Bellarmine.
pass_b_english: Someone may say justice itself required God to will the imputation of that first sin rather than of other sins. Then why, I ask, was that cause never produced? Why call God's will the unique cause of the matter? And how — while we for now only answer — will anyone prove that justice required it? Flee to our conjunction with Adam, and was that bond stronger at his first sin than later, or stronger with him than with parents nearer to us? Flee to some unknown covenant whose terms were that, if he sinned, his first sin would be charged to all his posterity under those two penalties — inherent sin and eternal death — and that covenant must be proved from Scripture, which cannot be done at all. Above all we must beware of ascribing to God anything Scripture does not give Him, especially anything that clouds His virtues; for that cannot fail to be a grave sin.
source_text: Sed fortasse exigebat justitia, ut Deus vellet primum illud peccatum imputare potius quam alia peccata? Cur ergo, inquam, hanc causam non attulit? cur dixit illius rei unicam esse causam, Dei voluntatem? Aut quomodo probabitur (nos enim nunc quidem respondentium partes tuemur) id justitiam exegisse? Si confugias ad conjunctionem quae nobis cum Adamo intercedit, ea ne major fuit cum primum peccaret quam postea, aut cum eo, quam cum propinquioribus nostris parentibus? Si ad nescio quoddam foedus, cujus haec fuerit conditio, ut si peccaret, primum eius peccatum omnibus eius posteris ad duas istas poenas imputaretur, peccatum inhaerens & mortem aeternam, probandum erit illud foedus e Scriptura; id quod est prorsus impossibile. Cavendum est autem nobis quam diligentissime ne quid praeter Scripturam Deo tribuamus, praesertim ejusmodi, quod virtutes eius obscuret; id enim non potest non grave peccatum esse.

choices.decision: Garissoles named will alone; justice-demand unproved
unknown federal condition cannot be proved from Scripture
